description: Dramatic cliff-top architecture with the iconic sunset cabana, private pool villas, and sustainable luxury.
tipsAndTricks: The sunset cabana is the most photographed spot in Bali — book it for golden hour.
The kids' eco-program includes recycling crafts and organic gardening.
Request villa 11 for the best ocean views and privacy.

parentStory.title: The cabana that changed everything
parentStory.excerpt: We got engaged at sunset. And the kids loved the kids club.
parentStory.author: Aisha
parentStory.fullStory: We came for our anniversary and the sunset cabana was everything. Our two kids spent the evening with the amazing kids club staff making Batik paintings while we watched the sun sink into the Indian Ocean with cocktails. Perfect balance of romance and family.

name: Rosewood Phnom Penh
description: Luxury atop Vattanac Capital Tower with skyline views, Cambodia's finest dining, and Art Deco Indochine elegance.
tipsAndTricks: The sky bar on the 37th floor has incredible sunset views over the Mekong.
Books, the hotel library café, is perfect for a quiet family afternoon.
Ask the concierge to arrange a private tuk-tuk food tour.

parentStory.title: Cambodia's new crown jewel
parentStory.excerpt: We felt like royalty in the capital.
parentStory.author: Nathan
parentStory.fullStory: Rosewood Phnom Penh is effortlessly elegant. The staff welcomed our kids with a personalised scavenger hunt through the hotel. The infinity pool overlooks the entire city. We took a private boat to the floating villages and came back to the best Khmer curry of our lives at the hotel.

safetyNote: High-rise hotel (levels 35+) with pool accessible by elevator. Street-level chaos in Phnom Penh for strollers.

name: Amanoi
description: Aman's first Vietnamese resort on the dramatic Ninh Thuan coastline with Lotus Pavilion spa and national park access.
location: Vinh Hy Bay, Ninh Thuan, Vietnam
tipsAndTricks: The Lotus Pavilion spa is one of Aman's best — book the family treatment.
Take the guided hike through Nui Chua National Park.
Cliff pool villas have the most dramatic ocean views in Vietnam.

parentStory.title: Hidden paradise on the Vietnamese coast
parentStory.excerpt: We felt like the first people to discover this bay.
parentStory.author: Liam
parentStory.fullStory: Amanoi is reached via a winding mountain road, and the reveal when you first see Vinh Hy Bay is breathtaking. Our pavilion was perched on the cliffside overlooking the turquoise bay. The kids did a marine biology program with the naturalist. We did nothing but read, swim, and eat. Perfect.

name: Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi
description: An island kingdom of 122 villas across three private islands with 11 dining venues and the largest spa in the Maldives.
tipsAndTricks: The Stella Maris Ocean Villa has a glass-floored living room over the lagoon.
Book the Zuma tasting menu for one royal adult dinner.
The kids club has a mini marine biology program.

parentStory.title: Three islands of pure luxury
parentStory.excerpt: My daughter said this was better than the cartoons she usually prefers.
parentStory.author: Amanda
parentStory.fullStory: Three private islands connected by bridges felt like our own kingdom. The overwater villa had a glass floor where we watched reef sharks swim beneath us every morning. The kids club was so good our 5-year-old asked to go back after lunch. We had the best sushi of our lives at Zuma.

name: Safari World Bangkok
description: Massive open zoo and marine park with drive-through safari, animal shows, and feeding experiences. Perfect for animal-loving families with spacious areas and good facilities.
location: 99 Panya Intra Rd, Sam Wa Tawan Tok, Khlong Sam Wa, Bangkok 10510
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds at Safari World Bangkok.
Best time to go is early morning before the heat sets in.
Bring water and snacks — prices inside can be steep.

parentStory.title: Lunch with the giraffes
parentStory.excerpt: My three-year-old fed a giraffe and hasn't stopped talking about it.
parentStory.author: Priya
parentStory.fullStory: I was sceptical about Safari World. Another tourist trap, I thought. But watching my daughter's face light up as a giraffe gently took a banana from her hand — that was worth the entire trip. The drive-through safari section means even the littlest ones stay strapped in comfortably. We spent four hours and could've stayed four more.

name: Sea Life Bangkok Ocean World
description: Southeast Asia's largest aquarium located under Siam Paragon mall. Walk-through tunnels, touch pools, and penguin feeding shows. Air-conditioned and stroller-friendly.
location: Siam Paragon, 991 Rama I Rd, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds at Sea Life Bangkok Ocean World.
Best time to go is early morning before the heat sets in.
Bring water and snacks — prices inside can be steep.

parentStory.title: Air-conditioned sanity
parentStory.excerpt: When Bangkok heat gets too much, this aquarium saves the day.
parentStory.author: Mei-Lin
parentStory.fullStory: Bangkok in April is brutal with kids. We ducked into Siam Paragon for lunch and stumbled into Sea Life. The underwater tunnel had both kids mesmerised for twenty minutes straight. The touch pool where they could feel starfish and sea cucumbers was their favourite. Two hours of cool, calm, happy children. A miracle.

klook.text: Klook Sea Life Bangkok Ocean World

name: KidZania Bangkok
description: Interactive role-playing city where kids can try over 80 professions. Located in Siam Paragon with English-speaking staff and excellent safety standards.
location: 5th Floor, Siam Paragon, 991 Rama I Rd, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds at KidZania Bangkok.
Best time to go is early morning before the heat sets in.
Bring water and snacks — prices inside can be steep.

parentStory.title: They didn't want to leave
parentStory.excerpt: My son the firefighter, my daughter the pilot — all in one afternoon.
parentStory.author: David
parentStory.fullStory: KidZania is genius. You walk in and suddenly your kids aren't bored — they're pilots, firefighters, chefs, doctors. Everything is scaled down but real: actual fire trucks, working model planes, a hospital with pretend patients. My kids learned about earning a salary (KidZos) and managing money without even realising it. The English-speaking staff were patient and encouraging. The grown-up seating area with coffee was a nice bonus.

name: Dream World Bangkok
description: Thailand's answer to Disneyland with themed zones, gentle rides for young children, and thrilling rides for teens. Good mix of indoor and outdoor attractions.
location: 62 Moo 1, Rangsit-Nakornnayok Rd, Thanyaburi, Pathum Thani 12130
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds at Dream World Bangkok.
Best time to go is early morning before the heat sets in.
Bring water and snacks — prices inside can be steep.

parentStory.title: Thailand's answer to Disney
parentStory.excerpt: Half the price, still plenty of magic.
parentStory.author: Sarah
parentStory.fullStory: Dream World doesn't have the Disney polish, but what it lacks in Pixar it makes up for in sheer fun. The snow room — actual snow in Bangkok — was a highlight for kids who'd never touched it. Rides range from gentle teacups for toddlers to legit roller coasters for teens. We went on a Thursday and barely queued. Bring snacks from 7-Eleven to avoid the overpriced food court.

name: Chatuchak Weekend Market (Kid-Friendly Areas)
description: World's largest weekend market with dedicated kid-friendly sections. Pet zone, toy sections, kid clothing, and family-friendly food courts. Go early to avoid heat.
tipsAndTricks: Visit on weekdays to avoid crowds at Chatuchak Weekend Market (Kid-Friendly Areas).
Best time to go is early morning before the heat sets in.
Bring water and snacks — prices inside can be steep.

parentStory.title: Market mission with kids
parentStory.excerpt: The pet zone alone is worth the trip.
parentStory.author: Alex
parentStory.fullStory: Taking kids to a market with 15,000 stalls sounds insane, but hear me out. Go early — 9am — before the heat and crowds. Head straight to Section 13 for the pet area. My kids spent an hour watching puppies, bunnies, and hamsters. The toy section in Section 5 has cheap bubble guns and kites that kept them entertained all afternoon. Bring a stroller for the unavoidable nap, and you'll be fine.

safetyNote: Very crowded on weekends, hot with limited shade, street traffic adjacent. Kids can easily wander off in the maze-like aisles.

name: Six Senses Kyoto
description: Zen-inspired urban sanctuary with organic spa and family-friendly onsens.
tipsAndTricks: Book family tea ceremony 1 week ahead.
Bamboo forest walk at sunrise before crowds.
Kids eat free at organic restaurant.

parentStory.title: Finding Zen with toddlers
parentStory.excerpt: My 3yo found inner peace making miso.
parentStory.author: Mia Chen
parentStory.fullStory: I was nervous traveling to Kyoto with a toddler and a moody 7-year-old, but Six Senses Kyoto turned our trip into a spiritual awakening. While I attended sunrise yoga overlooking the Higashiyama hills, my kids were making organic miso with the chef in a tiny kitchen designed just for them. By the end of our stay, my youngest had learned to bow before meals, and my older child actually asked for meditation time. It was the first vacation where I felt as nourished as the children.

name: Capella Okinawa
description: Tropical Japanese paradise with aqua park and dolphin encounters.
tipsAndTricks: Dolphin program books out 2 weeks in advance.
Pack reef-safe sunscreen for marine activities.
Take the glass-bottom boat if kids are scared to snorkel.

parentStory.title: Dolphin dreams do come true
parentStory.excerpt: My 6yo touched a dolphin and cried happy tears.
parentStory.author: Kenji Tanaka
parentStory.fullStory: Okinawa surprised us in ways I never expected. Capella's dolphin encounter program wasn't just a splash-and-go experience; it was an educational journey where marine biologists taught my kids about ocean conservation while they fed and touched a Pacific bottlenose dolphin. My daughter, who had been afraid of deep water, found her courage on the glass-bottom boat, pointing at coral reefs with unbridled joy. The kids left not just with memories, but with a genuine love for the ocean.

name: Aman Niseko
description: Hokkaido powder paradise with ski-in/ski-out family suites and onsen.
tipsAndTricks: Book ski school 2 months ahead during peak season.
Family onsens are bookable privately — reserve daily.
Summer offers hiking and river rafting for older kids.

parentStory.title: Powder day for everyone
parentStory.excerpt: My 4yo skied her first blue run with a grin.
parentStory.author: Sarah Williams
parentStory.fullStory: Hokkaido's legendary powder is amazing enough, but it was the ski-in, ski-out magic at Aman Niseko that made this our best family winter vacation. Each morning we'd glide from our suite straight onto the slopes, with my youngest in ski school learning from instructors who were impossibly patient. My husband and I stole afternoon runs together while the kids enjoyed hot chocolate in the family lounge, and the onsen at sunset became our daily ritual. The hot stone spa after a day in the snow was pure heaven.

name: Six Senses Krabi Island
description: Cliff-backed island sanctuary with limestone karst views and family villas.
tipsAndTricks: Island hopping to Phi Phi leaves early — pack snacks.
Book the rock climbing experience for kids 8+.
Pool villa with direct lagoon access is best for toddlers.

parentStory.title: Where karst meets family
parentStory.excerpt: We kayaked into emerald caves as a family of four.
parentStory.author: Natalie Hernandez
parentStory.fullStory: The Andaman Sea at sunset from our pool villa at Six Senses Krabi Island was everything we dreamed of and more. We spent our mornings kayaking through emerald lagoons, navigating between limestone karsts that looked like they belonged on another planet. My 8-year-old son became a junior explorer, collecting shells and learning about mangrove ecosystems from the resident naturalist. Even our toddler found joy in the shallow lagoon pool, splashing while the staff brought fresh coconut water. It was raw nature wrapped in six-star comfort.

name: Mandarin Oriental Bangkok
description: Iconic riverside heritage hotel with legendary service and family programs.
tipsAndTricks: Authors' Lounge high tea is a must — book 1 week ahead.
Book the Chao Phraya dinner cruise from the hotel pier.
Kids cooking class teaches Thai spring rolls — perfect for 5+.

parentStory.title: A century of family tradition
parentStory.excerpt: My mother stayed here in 1985 and I just continued the legacy.
parentStory.author: James Patterson
parentStory.fullStory: My mother visited the Mandarin Oriental Bangkok in 1985 and spoke of it with such reverence that I knew I had to bring my own family one day. Walking through those iconic lobby doors with my wife and two daughters felt like stepping into living history, but the staff made us feel like it was our own private home. The kids were treated to a teddy bear picnic on the lawn while my wife and I enjoyed cocktails at the Bamboo Bar. Three generations of our family have now fallen in love with this remarkable hotel.

name: Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai Hoi An
description: Vietnamese beachfront masterpiece with overwater spa and cultural workshops.
tipsAndTricks: Take the free shuttle to Hoi An Ancient Town in the evening.
Lantern-making workshop is included for kids under 12.
Book the Chef's Table for a family-friendly degustation.

parentStory.title: Lanterns and memories
parentStory.excerpt: My 7yo made a lantern that now hangs in our living room.
parentStory.author: Amanda Reed
parentStory.fullStory: The Nam Hai exceeded every expectation we had for a Vietnamese family escape. Our villa opened onto a pristine stretch of Ha My Beach, where my kids spent hours building sandcastles while I enjoyed a Vietnamese coffee delivered to my lounger. The cultural immersion was incredible — my daughter made silk lanterns in a workshop that rivaled any art class she'd taken at home, and my son learned to roll fresh spring rolls from a chef who treated him like an apprentice. We left Hoi An with suitcases full of memories and one very special lantern.

itineraryComparison.fullDay: Hoi An Old Town + Lantern Making

name: Signiel Seoul
description: Soaring skyscraper luxury on floors 81-99 with panoramic Seoul views.
tipsAndTricks: Lotte World theme park is connected underground — perfect rainy day.
Book a window table at 81 Restaurant for sunset over Seoul.
Ask for a high floor for the best views; south-facing rooms see the Han River.

parentStory.title: Above the clouds with kids
parentStory.excerpt: We had breakfast at 1,000 feet and my kids didn't touch a screen all day.
parentStory.author: Jennifer Park
parentStory.fullStory: Riding the elevator to the 81st floor of Signiel Seoul with my 5 and 7-year-old, I wondered if they'd be bored at a hotel so high in the sky. Instead, they spent the entire visit with their noses pressed against the floor-to-ceiling windows, spotting landmarks across Seoul. The hotel's connection to Lotte World Tower meant we skipped lines at the observation deck, and the kids club had the best K-craft activities I've ever seen. My husband and I even enjoyed a Michelin-starred dinner while the hotel's nanny service read bedtime stories to our children.

name: Jeju Shinhwa World Hotels & Resorts (Landing Conference)
description: Massive family entertainment complex with water park, theme park, and luxury hotels.
tipsAndTricks: Buy the 3-day park pass — it saves 30% over single tickets.
The water park has a dedicated toddler zone.
Spring for the Landing Resort wing — it's adults-only quiet by night.

parentStory.title: Jeju's answer to family fun
parentStory.excerpt: We didn't leave the complex for 4 days and no one complained.
parentStory.author: Michael Kim
parentStory.fullStory: I'll admit I was skeptical about an integrated resort in Jeju, but Shinhwa World proved me wrong in the best way. The moment we checked into the Landing Conference hotel, my kids spotted the giant water slides through the window and started jumping with excitement. We spent four full days without leaving the complex — mornings at the theme park, afternoons at the water park, and evenings exploring Jeju's volcanic coastline. The butler even arranged a last-minute tangerine picking tour that became the highlight of our trip.

name: Ceylon Tea Trails
description: Five colonial-era tea planter bungalows on a working tea estate in the Ceylon highlands.
tipsAndTricks: Book the Tientsin bungalow for the best sunrise views.
Tea-picking experience is best at 6am before the heat.
Pack layers — it gets cool in the highlands at night.

parentStory.title: Sipping tea at 4,000 feet
parentStory.excerpt: My city kids learned where tea actually comes from.
parentStory.author: Priya Fernando
parentStory.fullStory: Our children, born and raised in Singapore, had never seen a tea leaf in their lives before Ceylon Tea Trails. Arriving at the Castlereagh bungalow, surrounded by emerald tea bushes stretching to the horizon, they stared in wonder. An early morning walk with the tea master revealed the entire journey from leaf to cup — my 10-year-old was so fascinated she took notes. The evenings were spent playing board games by the fireplace, disconnected from screens, connected to each other. It was the most peaceful family vacation we've ever had.

itineraryComparison.fullDay: Full Tea Estate Tour + Cooking Class

name: Aman Sanya
description: Hainan island retreat on a private cove with Chinese courtyard architecture and holistic wellness.
tipsAndTricks: Book the Chinese medicine consultation for a unique family experience.
Sanya's Yalong Bay Tropical Paradise Park is a 20-minute drive.
Ask for a Courtyard Suite — kids love the private garden.

parentStory.title: Hainan's hidden Aman gem
parentStory.excerpt: We found a piece of paradise on China's Hawaii.
parentStory.author: Thomas Wei
parentStory.fullStory: Aman Sanya surprised me with how seamlessly it blended Chinese heritage with tropical resort living. Our courtyard suite opened onto a private garden where my children practiced tai chi with a master who somehow made it fun for 6-year-olds. The private cove beach was powder-soft and almost empty, and the Kids Club introduced my kids to Chinese brush painting and calligraphy. My wife and I stole moments at the library pavilion overlooking the South China Sea, reading in silence — the rarest luxury of all for parents.
